summary: Lane County tower built 1934 (70 ft, or 86 ft per one source), cut to 45 ft in 1955, removed 1971 or abandoned 1972; now gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 70-ft wooden tower with 7x7-ft cab built 1934; cut to 45 ft with a live-in cab added in 1955
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1972 and now gone; Forest Lookouts says it was removed in 1971. Sources disagree on the 1934 height (70 ft or 86 ft).

events.note: Road being pushed up the mountain; a 1933 field report says a nearby camp should, if possible, stay to finish the road and build the tower and lookout house.
Wooden tower with 7x7-ft cab. firelookout.com and firetower.org give 70 ft; Forest Lookouts gives 86 ft and says Wendling CCC members built it.
Charles Kingsley named as lookout at the Castle Rock station in press reports.
August 1935 report from the lookout that the hills seemed alive with flames.
Trail of about half a mile built from the lookout to a spring; before that water came from a CCC road about 3.5 miles away.
Mosby Creek CCC spike camp had built ten miles of road to the tower since June 15, 1939.
Forest Guard Bob Wagner reported a four-day-old, 700-acre blaze under control.
Ronald Byers transferred to Castle Rock from the Mt. Nebo post.
Tower cut to 45 ft with a live-in cab added.
Observation cab found unsafe; finished that fall for materials costing $450.
Copper lightning-protection wire stolen; the thief was convicted and placed on probation.
Forest Lookouts says the lookout was removed in 1971.
Abandoned in 1972; the tower is now gone according to firetower.org and firelookout.com.
Registered November 18, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek.

corrections.why: Two sources describe the 1934 tower as 70 ft (21.3 m). The 26.2 m figure matches only the 86-ft figure on the Forest Lookouts page. The tower was cut to 45 ft (13.7 m) in 1955.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org and firelookout.com give 70 ft for the 1934 tower; Forest Lookouts gives 86 ft. The facts use 70 ft (21.3 m); the story reports both.
Forest Lookouts says the lookout was removed in 1971; firetower.org and firelookout.com say it was abandoned in 1972 and is now gone. The story reports both dates.

Forest Lookouts files the site as Castle Rock (Bear Mountain); the register and firelookout.com call it Bear (Castle) Mountain. The Forest Lookouts section describes the same Eastern Lane station and the same mountain, so it is treated as one site.

notes_for_editor: Access is left out: no source says whether the land is open to the public, so the brief's unknown stands. No source describes remains or a view at the site now; the story says so. The brief's 26.2 m height matches only the Forest Lookouts 86-ft figure. firelookout.org lists a different Castle Rock (FFLOS US 944, Lane County, 44.15131, -122.21206); that is a separate site and was not merged. Lookout names Charles Kingsley and Bob Wagner come from 1935 and 1940 press items quoted on Forest Lookouts; they were not checked against the newspapers.
